newsitem.title: CANADA: Service bid puts Loewen back in spotlight.
newsitem.headline: Service bid puts Loewen back in spotlight.

text.p: A hostile takeover bid for Canada's Loewen Group Inc has pushed North America's second-biggest funeral company back into the spotlight after a brush with bankruptcy earlier this year.
Service Corp International, the continent's number one funeral home operator, launched an unsolicited bid for Loewen on Tuesday valued at US$2.5 billion.
While Loewen said it is reviewing the "unsolicited proposal", analysts said Service Corp will likely have to sweeten its bid for the Vancouver-based company.
"There offer doesn't look particularly generous because in my view they (Loewen) should get there anyway," said David Brodie, an analyst with CIBC Wood Gundy.
Brodie said his 12-month price target for Loewen's stock was US$42.50, excluding a takeover premium.
Service Corp said it is willing to increase its offer after performing a due diligence review.
Loewen's stock rose sharply on both Canadian and U.S. stock exchanges after the bid was announced. It closed up 8.45 at 54.95 after reaching a new high of 57 on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
On Nasdaq, Loewen's stock finished 6-1/4 higher at 40 on 2.7 million shares. It earlier reached a peak of 42-1/2.
"The Loewen board indicated that they will review the proposal and respond in due course. Beyond that we can't say very much," said Loewen spokesman Thomas Franco.
The takeover offer comes as Loewen recovers from a brush with bankruptcy last January due to a US$500 million damage award in a U.S. breach-of-contract case.
Days before filing for bankruptcy protection, Loewen reached a US$175 million out-of-court settlement with the plaintiff, a Mississippi funeral home operator.
The costly legal battle put Loewen's aggressive acquisition strategy on hold until June when it acquired Prime Succession Inc, the largest privately held funeral home operator in the United States.
Loewen joined forces with merchant bank Blackstone Group to buy Prime for US$295 million.

Analysts said there appear to be no obvious rival bidders for Loewen. "Within the industry it appears to be a longshot," another analyst said, noting that the number three operator, Stewart Enterprises Inc, is one-third the size of Loewen which would make it a difficult undertaking.
"It's not obvious in terms of other players. Stewart would be the only one which could potentially do it in North America, but it would be fairly large," Brodie said.
Analysts said Loewen could search for financial investors to help fend off Service Corp and allow the current management to stay in control.
